summary: Intermittent dedicated throughput oscillation traced to tenant-side metrics exporter spike
description: Customer reports recurring 10-30 minute windows of severe throughput oscillation on their dedicated pool in us-east. P50 remains stable but p95/p99 throughput drops ~70% during windows, with increased attach latency and GPU allocation failures. Symptoms surfaced first 2026-03-11 09:40 UTC and recurred intermittently. Customer is on a reserved dedicated pool; impacts multiple production routes. Initial suspect is autoscaler hysteresis, but telemetry suggests an external signal correlating with the windows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs steady production traffic to reserved dedicated pool (AtlasAI flow).
2) Observe normal throughput for ~20-40 minutes, then sudden oscillation window (10-30 minutes) where batched route throughput drops and queued latency rises.
3) During window, allocator logs show temporary attach timeouts and GPU slot unavailability, despite cluster having nominal spare capacity.
4) Issue self-recovers after window; pattern repeats multiple times per day.
5) Customer reproduced once by enabling high-frequency metrics export from their sidecar (push every 250ms) which correlated with an immediate onset of a window.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Noisy tenant sidecar (rapid metrics exporter) causes local CPU and socket saturation on node, leading to delayed heartbeat and delayed prefetch acknowledgements; allocator interprets as slot not ready and throttles attach.

Hypothesis B: Rapid small-metric pushes create NVLink scheduling contention (observed upstream with mixed-precision loads) causing transient gpu_io_wait which reduces effective throughput and triggers autoscaler conservative fallback.
Checked Grafana dashboard: allocation failure spikes align with sidecar cpu spikes and high kernel-scheduling wait on selected nodes (node-uss-east-41a/b).
Reproduced locally in staging by instrumenting a client to push metrics at 200-300ms intervals; reproduced attach timeouts and batched route serialization.
comments: Support (Aisha): Customer reported first occurrence after rolling a new sidecar that increased metrics frequency. Asked customer to revert to previous sidecar version for mitigation 2026-03-11 12:10 UTC.

SRE (Miguel): Probed node metrics and observed elevated softirq and netdev queues during windows. Opened ephemeral ssh session to node-uss-east-41a; collected top, iostat, nvidia-smi samples 2026-03-12 02:20 UTC.
Customer (AtlasAI-SRE): Confirmed they shipped a telemetry change on 2026-03-11 that increased metrics push cadence. Agrees to throttle back metric frequency as workaround 2026-03-12 03:05 UTC.
Eng (Runtime team): Noted that autoscaler was overly conservative when node heartbeat RTT > 10s; proposal to relax hysteresis while we identify root cause (linked PR).
actions_taken: Applied temporary mitigation: network policer rule to limit sidecar metrics egress to 1/s for tenant atlasai (traffic-shaping) 2026-03-12 04:00 UTC.
Escalated to Runtime and Autoscaler teams; assigned debugging spike to Miguel and runtime eng 2026-03-12 05:00 UTC.
Placed customer routes on fallback compatible model variants to preserve latency-sensitive flows during next window 2026-03-12 06:10 UTC.
Created a short-term alert on node softirq and sidecar push rate correlation for dedicated pools 2026-03-12 07:00 UTC.
resolution: Workaround implemented: restricted high-frequency metrics pushes from AtlasAI sidecar and applied traffic shaping at edge. After throttling metrics to 1/s and reverting sidecar version, dedicated pool throughput stabilized and attach timeouts stopped. Long-term fixes: Runtime team to add backpressure handling for noisy sidecars and autoscaler team to relax one specific heartbeat hysteresis threshold (see PR github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/1182). Follow-up action items open in linked Confluence page for permanent remediation.
follow_up_items: Runtime: add per-tenant sidecar push-rate detection and soft-drop to avoid node-level saturation (owner: runtime-team)
Autoscaler: evaluate relaxing heartbeat hysteresis when spare GPU capacity detected (owner: autoscaler-team)
Customer success: communicate best-practice telemetry cadence for dedicated pools and add to onboarding docs (owner: CS)
